name: OpenAI Codex
summary: A general-purpose coding agent for reading, editing, running commands, and reviewing code in a local repository.
detail: Useful as the main code execution loop for a game project: break down gameplay, maintain scripts, run builds, and inspect failures. Engine integration still requires a CLI, editor bridge, or MCP server; compiling successfully does not establish that a game is playable.

name: Claude Code
summary: A coding agent that reads and edits projects, runs tools, and supports skills, hooks, and MCP through terminal and IDE interfaces.
detail: Can develop game scripts, migrate architecture, troubleshoot builds, and connect to Unity, Godot, or UE through community MCP servers. Use CLAUDE.md, skills, and editor state together; one MCP demonstration does not establish complete engine automation.

name: Gemini CLI
summary: Google's open-source terminal coding agent with file access, shell tools, extensions, and MCP support.
detail: Can help understand game projects, edit scripts, and drive editors through MCP. At the recorded source check, the official repository directed some users to Antigravity CLI and noted differences in support for newer models. Choose an entry point based on your account and the official migration guidance.

name: DeepSeek · Agent Integrations
summary: Official guidance for using DeepSeek as a model backend within agent harnesses such as Claude Code.
detail: The Anthropic API compatibility layer connects DeepSeek to existing tool loops. The chosen harness handles files, tests, and engine connections. Keep the model separate from the execution framework: the compatibility documentation lists ignored or unsupported fields, so equivalent capabilities should not be assumed.

name: OpenCode
summary: An open-source coding agent with multiple model providers, Plan / Build modes, and project instructions.
detail: Useful for turning game requirements into a plan, then editing C#, GDScript, TypeScript, or C++ projects. Providers and models can be selected independently; launching an editor, inspecting visuals, and validating gameplay still require the appropriate tools.

name: Cline
summary: An open-source coding agent with multiple models, Plan / Act modes, project rules, and MCP support.
detail: Useful for reviewing and editing game code in an IDE or CLI, with build output and MCP editor tools in the feedback loop. Reuse .clinerules and skills to capture engine conventions; editor operations depend on the specific bridge service.

name: Aider
summary: A terminal AI pair-programming tool built around repository maps, Git changes, and lint and test feedback.
detail: Useful for changes across files, refactoring, and testable logic in existing game projects, with model options including DeepSeek. Its code editing workflow does not directly control Unity, UE, or Blender editors; visual feedback needs a separate setup.

name: OpenHands · Agent Canvas
summary: An open-source development console for managing local, remote, and cloud agent environments.
detail: Can centralize multi-agent tasks, environments, and execution records for game projects. The repository provides the Agent Canvas frontend and orchestration entry point; the core tool loop and Agent Server live in a separate SDK repository. Game automation still requires engine tools.

name: OpenHands Software Agent SDK
summary: A programmable development framework for agents, tools, conversations, workspaces, and server interfaces.
detail: Useful for game development experiments: wrap builds, scene inspections, and tests as tools for a coding agent, and record execution in local or container workspaces. The SDK supports custom workflows and tools; it does not include a semantic layer for every game engine.

name: Claude Agent SDK
summary: Embed Claude Code's tool loop, permissions, sessions, and extensions in Python or TypeScript applications.
detail: Can power game-specific code repair, content validation, or engine MCP orchestration services, with hooks recording execution evidence. It serves a different role from the Client SDK for direct model calls; domain tools, scoring rules, and runtime environments must still be supplied.

name: mini-swe-agent
summary: A minimal shell-based coding-agent research baseline designed for modification and trace inspection.
detail: Useful for isolating model, prompt, and environment effects in game code generation and repair, or wrapping commands such as Godot headless. It is a general software engineering agent rather than a game benchmark; playability, visuals, and physics require additional validation.

name: AGENTS.md
summary: An open Markdown format for giving coding agents build commands, test rules, and project conventions.
detail: Game projects can record engine versions, launch commands, directory rules, asset import conventions, and acceptance checks to reduce environment guesswork. This is a project instruction format rather than an agent runtime; discovery and configuration vary by client.

name: Agent Skills
summary: An open format that packages domain workflows as SKILL.md instructions, scripts, and reference materials.
detail: Useful for repeatable game tasks such as sprite normalization, GLB export, scene inspection, and regression testing, with domain knowledge loaded as needed. Skills provide procedures and resources; engine control still requires tools, dependencies, and a compatible client.

name: Codex · Create Browser-based Games
summary: OpenAI's browser game workflow covering planning, project instructions, asset generation, and browser iteration.
detail: Define the player goal, core loop, inputs, and win and loss conditions, then implement with PLAN.md and AGENTS.md. Combine image skills and Playwright for visual and interaction feedback. This is a practical guide, not a performance guarantee for every game genre or a research benchmark.

name: MCP for Unity
summary: A community MCP bridge connecting general-purpose coding agents to the Unity Editor.
detail: Exposes editor operations for scenes, GameObjects, C# scripts, assets, and tests, giving agents access to state that text-only code edits cannot reveal. The project is explicitly independent of Unity Technologies; validate changes with compilation logs, screenshots, and PlayMode tests.

name: Unity-MCP Operator Guide
summary: A practical skill in the MCP for Unity repository: inspect editor state, act, wait for compilation, and verify results.
detail: Defines a resource-first approach to scene operations, plus compilation waits, console checks, and screenshot verification after script edits. It can serve as a Unity agent operating procedure. The skill requires MCP for Unity; examples and parameters vary with Unity, UI, and input system versions.

name: Godot MCP · Coding-Solo
summary: A community MCP server for launching Godot, running projects, reading logs, and performing basic scene operations.
detail: Supports project execution, debug output capture, scene and node creation, Sprite2D texture loading, and some 3D MeshLibrary operations. It can give agents feedback from real projects; these interfaces do not provide complete visual playtesting or every editor feature. At the checked commit, the server keeps one active project process and sends kill before spawning another without awaiting prior exit. Stop returns after sending a kill request rather than waiting for process exit; natural exit clears the handle used by get_debug_output. Archive output separately for reliable crash evidence.

name: MCP for Blender
summary: A Blender add-on and MCP server for agent-driven modeling, materials, Python execution, and visual feedback.
detail: Useful as a bridge for 3D game asset production and scene prototypes, with viewport feedback for geometry, materials, and layout. Previously named blender-mcp, the repository and package have been renamed. This is a third-party community integration; check topology, scale, UVs, collision, and export compatibility.

name: Unreal MCP · chongdashu
summary: A Python MCP server and UE C++ plugin connecting agents to Actors, Blueprints, and viewport controls.
detail: Covers Actor transforms, Blueprint classes and components, some node graphs, and editor camera operations for UE scene and gameplay prototypes. The author explicitly marks it experimental and advises against production use; pin compatible versions and verify the supported operations individually.

name: Playwright MCP
summary: Microsoft's browser automation MCP server for exposing page structure, interactions, and browser feedback to agents.
detail: Useful for browser game menus, HUDs, launch flows, and web interactions, combined with screenshots, keyboard input, and game debug interfaces. The default mode relies on structured accessibility trees; internal Canvas and WebGL gameplay state needs additional observation. The project also offers a CLI + Skills workflow.
